concepts.name: The Smooth Manifold
concepts.summary: A manifold is a space that is globally curved but locally flat: every point has a small neighbourhood indistinguishable from ordinary flat space, where usual arithmetic and geometry apply, while the whole surface bends and closes seamlessly like a globe. Many sets of valid arrangements form such curved surfaces. (Upstairs: these become the spaces of orientation and motion.)

concepts.name: Turns Form a Curved Space
concepts.summary: The set of all turns (rotations about a fixed centre) is itself a smooth curved surface. Planar turns need one number, the angle, which wraps around: they form a circle, one degree of freedom. Turns in space need three numbers: they form a three-dimensional curved surface. A 3D turn is written as a 3×3 grid of nine numbers, but rigid constraints leave only three free, so one cannot perturb a single entry and remain a valid turn — nine numbers, three freedoms. (Upstairs: this is the geometry of orientation.)
